title: Wasteland
build: Electronic Arts disk release, two double-sided disks as four G64 side images; play copies made with the game's own Copy utility

records.c: The start-up's first instruction, where the boot file 2.0 jumps once it has loaded T4/L16 (16 pages) to $7E00-$8DFF: JMP startup_main ($7F2A). The program carries no load header; it is not started through the engine's load_program.

Starts sound record X (0, 11, 22 or 33: an offset into sound_records at $7E4B, 11 bytes a record) on the SID voice whose registers begin at $D400+Y (Y = 0 voice 1, 7 voice 2): control $D404+Y = 0 (gate off), frequency $D400/$D401+Y = record bytes 8/9, master volume $D418 = byte 10, $D415+Y-$D417+Y = bytes 5-7, pulse width $D402/$D403+Y = bytes 3/4, attack/decay $D405+Y = byte 0, sustain/release $D406+Y = byte 1, and last control $D404+Y = byte 2, which starts the note. With Y = 7 bytes 5-7 land at $D41C-$D41E, beyond the filter and volume registers $D415-$D418. Callers: siren_sound ($7E7B, $7E82), whistle_sound ($7EFE), explosion_sound ($7F17). X and Y kept.

Four 11-byte SID records for start_sound, at offsets X = 0, 11, 22, 33. Columns: 0 attack/decay ($D405+Y), 1 sustain/release ($D406+Y), 2 control ($D404+Y, written last), 3-4 pulse width low/high, 5-7 to $D415+Y-$D417+Y, 8-9 frequency low/high, 10 master volume ($D418). Record 0 (here to $7E55) is the explosion: attack/decay $1A, sustain/release 0, control $85 (noise, gate on), pulse width $07F3, $4E $22 $F0, frequency $0320, volume $0F. This byte is record 0's attack/decay; each column's first byte below carries the column's name.
Column 1 of sound_records, read as $7E4C+X ($7E3E): sustain/release, to $D406+Y. Record 0 holds 0: no sustain, the noise dies away with the decay.
Column 2 of sound_records ($7E4D+X, $7E44): the control byte, written last to $D404+Y so that its gate bit starts the note. Record 0: $85, noise waveform (bit 7) with the gate (bit 0) and bit 2 set.
Column 3 of sound_records ($7E4E+X, $7E2C): pulse width low byte, to $D402+Y. Record 0: $F3 (unused by its noise waveform).
Column 4 of sound_records ($7E4F+X, $7E32): pulse width high byte, to $D403+Y. Record 0: $07.
Column 5 of sound_records ($7E50+X, $7E1A): to $D415+Y, the filter cutoff's low register when Y = 0. Record 0: $4E.
Column 6 of sound_records ($7E51+X, $7E20): to $D416+Y, the filter cutoff's high register when Y = 0. Record 0: $22.
Column 7 of sound_records ($7E52+X, $7E26): to $D417+Y, the filter resonance and routing register when Y = 0. Record 0: $F0 (low nibble 0: no voice routed through the filter).
Column 8 of sound_records ($7E53+X, $7E08): frequency low byte, to $D400+Y. Record 0: $20.
Column 9 of sound_records ($7E54+X, $7E0E): frequency high byte, to $D401+Y. Record 0: $03, so the explosion's noise runs at frequency $0320.
Column 10 of sound_records ($7E55+X, $7E14): the master volume, written to $D418 whatever the voice. Record 0: $0F, full volume.

Sound record 1 (X = $0B), the siren's lower voice, started on voice 1 by siren_sound: attack/decay $BF, sustain/release $FF, control $21 (sawtooth, gate on), pulse width $0CEC, $05 $07 $F0 to $D415-$D417, frequency $1C31 (bytes 8-9 at $7E5E, which siren_sound also reads as its starting pitch) and volume $0A ($7E60).
Record 1's frequency low byte, $31: siren_sound loads it into X ($7E85) as the low byte of the siren's starting pitch $1C31.
Record 1's frequency high byte, $1C: siren_sound loads it into Y ($7E88), the high byte of the starting pitch.
Record 1's volume byte, $0A: start_sound writes it to $D418, and siren_sound reads it again ($7ECE) as the first step of its fade, $D418 counted down from 10 to 0.

Sound record 2 (X = $16), the falling whistle (whistle_sound), on voice 1: attack/decay $09, sustain/release 0, control $15 (triangle, gate on, bit 2 set), pulse width $0C3E, $BF $05 $F0 to $D415-$D417, frequency $FD2E, whose high byte whistle_sound then steps down from $FD to $0B; volume $0F.

Sound record 3 (X = $21), the siren's upper voice, started on voice 2 (Y = 7) by siren_sound: the bytes of record 1 except the frequency, $2187 (bytes 8-9 at $7E74), which is also where the siren's rise stops. Its bytes 5-7 ($05 $07 $F0) go to $D41C-$D41E with Y = 7; its last byte, $7E76, the volume $0A.
Record 3's frequency low byte, $87: siren_sound's rise stops when X reaches it ($7E9F).
Record 3's frequency high byte, $21, compared with Y at $7EA4: the siren rises from $1C31 to $2187. The byte after it ($7E76) is record 3's volume, $0A, which start_sound writes to $D418.

A rising and falling two-voice tone, a siren by its shape, played after 'war erupts' (attract_loop $809F): record 1 on voice 1 and record 3 on voice 2 (start_sound); then the pitch X/Y rises one step at a time from $1C31 (siren_start_freq) until the count reaches $2187 (siren_top_freq; the last pitch set is $2186), each step set by set_siren_pitch (voice 2 $0556 above voice 1, then delay_a($19)) with one menu poll (poll_menu, X = 1); a pause of delay_x_times(8); a fall one step at a time from $2187 until the count reaches $1838 (the last pitch set is $1839); then the master volume $D418 counts down from record 1's $0A to 0 with delay_a($C0) between steps, and voices 1 and 2 are silenced. The fall's decrement (DEX, BNE, DEY at $7EB5-$7EB8) lowers the high byte when the low byte reaches 0 instead of when it wraps, so at each of the nine high-byte boundaries one step is 256 too low: $2101, $2000, $20FF instead of $2101, $2100, $20FF. The rise's INX, BNE, INY is right. The title keys act from inside the polls of the rise and the fall; the pause and the fade poll nothing, so a key pressed during either waits in $EC for the next poll: the fall's first, or set_gauge_wait's after the siren (attract_loop $80B1).
One step of the siren: voice 1 frequency $D400/$D401 = X/Y, voice 2 frequency $D407/$D408 = X/Y + $0556, then delay_a($19) (JMP $04F0). X and Y kept.

A falling whistle, played twice as the gauge fills (attract_loop $80C7, $80D9): record 2 on voice 1 (start_sound, X = $16, Y = 0), then the frequency high byte $D401 steps from $FD down to $0B with delay_a(8) between steps, then voice 1 is silenced (JMP silence_voice_1). No key is polled meanwhile.

One explosion: record 0 (noise, attack 1, decay $A, no sustain) started on voice 1 (start_sound, X = 0, Y = 0), then delay_a($80) (JMP $04F0). attract_loop sounds it 14 times at the intervals in explosion_delays.

Silences voice 2: Y = 7, then (the BIT $00A0 at $7F21 hides silence_voice_1's LDY #$00) A = 0 to $D404+Y, voice 2's control register $D40B. Called by siren_sound ($7EDF) and both menu handlers ($81DE, $81FD).
Silences voice 1: Y = 0, control $D404 = 0 (gate off); entered inside the BIT at $7F21. Called by siren_sound, whistle_sound, both menu handlers and the JSR at $80F2, which nothing reaches.

The start-up from the hand-over: SEI, CLD, stack at $01FF, CLI; zero page $02-$FF and the engine's variables $EE00-$F3FF cleared; colour $EB = $6F; bitmap mode with the screen on and 24 rows ($D011 = $37); the whole screen cleared (clear_window, columns 0-39, pixel rows 0-$BF), then the text window set to pixel rows 8-$77; $6A = 1 (the roster-shown flag, so show_message calls clear_message_area_once, $1EA9, which clears only while $C9 is 0; attract_loop's clear_text_area sets $C9 to 1 before the first show_message, and nothing in the title sets it back to 0); the menu bar (setup_title_menu); the picture area's colours (colour_picture_area); a frame from column 0, row 0 to column 37, row 17 (draw_frame); the gauge drawn empty (set_gauge, $FF); $D011 = $37 again. Then the logo: its font read from T4/L1-L0 to $CA00-$CBFF (read_pages), swapped in (swap_logo_font), logo_glyph_block printed at column 33, row 1 in colour $86 (window left edge $25 = 33, so each $0D returns there, and bottom $28 = $C0 meanwhile), swapped out. Then the title picture: T5/L16 read to $5A00 ($FD1D), $CE = $14 (20: the unpack reads T5/L16-L0 and T4/L20-L18) and unpack_stream ($04F3) to $8A00 with limit $A300; header byte 2 ($8A02) set to $20; $B8, $AC and $C5 = 1: $AC turns the picture animation on, and $C5 keeps animate_picture_tick from reloading a portrait or redrawing the portrait window over the title (engine $05C9). Falls into attract_loop.

The title sequence, repeated until a menu handler loads another program. Gauge empty and text area cleared; credits, messages 1-4, in the message area (show_title_message); the picture redrawn (animation on, start_picture $041F, colour_picture_area, animation off) and a wait of 64 units; typed over the picture at column 1 (type_message_at): 5 'Place : EARTH' row 1, 6 'Year  : 1998' row 3, 7 'Status: DEFCON 1' row 5, 10 units apart; a wait of 50; the picture redrawn; message 8 'Computer defense initiative activated.'; 30 units still, then 70 animated; the text area cleared and messages 9-12 ('Diplomatic solutions to the world's problems fail and war erupts as some madmen press ahead with their insane dreams.'); siren_sound; animation on; then the gauge and the bombs ($80B0 on). Every wait polls the keyboard (wait_with_menu), so S, U, RETURN, ',' and '.' act at any point.

Operand of the LDA # at $80AF: the gauge level for the next step, $40 first ($80AC), 8 less after each step ($80BA). From $80B1: six steps of set_gauge_wait ($40 down to $18, 4 units each, the counter in the operand at $80EE), then level $10 and whistle_sound, a wait of 4, level 8 (4 units), level 1 (the gauge full) and whistle_sound again; then the explosions: for each entry of explosion_delays until its $FF, wait that many units and explosion_sound.

Operand of the LDX # at $80ED: first the count of gauge steps (6, stored at $80A7, counted down at $80BD), then the index into explosion_delays (stored at $80DE). The INX/BNE after it always loops, since the $FF in the table ends the loop first; the JSR silence_voice_1 at $80F2 is never reached.

The last part of attract_loop, after the explosions: animation off, text area cleared, then typed over the picture at column 1, rows 1-5: messages 13-17 'Current condition: / High concentrations of / radiation produce random storms / and mutations. Somehow life / continues in the Wasteland!' (10 units after the first); a wait of 100 units; JMP attract_loop.
The waits before each of the 14 explosions, in wait_with_menu units (read at $80E1): 4 5 2 3 6 5 1 3 4 3 4 2 4 3, ended by $FF.
Clears the message area (rows 18-22) without a '(RETURN)' prompt first: $AF = 0, the engine's count of lines printed since a key, then JMP clear_message_area ($0320).

records.s: engine entry $0320 = clear_message_area (not a KERNAL vector here)

records.c: Draws the gauge at columns 38-39 at level A: $9F = A, then JMP $04E1 (the engine's $0AA1, the Geiger counter gauge of play): 18 - A/8 rows from row 17 upwards in glyphs $80/$82 with colour $62, the rest up to row 0 in glyphs $7E/$5B; A = $FF fills none, A = 1 all 18. The title raises it while the bombs fall: $FF, $40 to $18, $10, 8, 1.
set_gauge with A, then a wait of 4 units (wait_with_menu with X = 4; the BIT $0AA2 at $8153 hides wait_10's LDX #$0A). attract_loop's gauge steps ($80B1, $80D1).
Waits 10 units: LDX #$0A, entered inside the BIT at $8153, then on into wait_with_menu. Between the typed lines of attract_loop.

Waits X units (X = 0 gives 256), each unit 255 keyboard polls (poll_menu with X = $FF), so the title's keys work and the picture animates during the wait (read_key ticks the animation while $AC is set). The units left are kept in the operand at $815F.
Operand of the LDX # at $815E: wait_with_menu's units left, stored at $8156; the DEX/BNE after it runs the next unit, and the RTS ends the wait.

Polls the keyboard X times (X = 0 gives 256): read_key ($022A, which also waits a moment and ticks the picture animation), then menu_key ($02DE), which runs Start or Utils for S, U or RETURN and moves the bar's selection for ',' and '.'. The polls left are kept in the operand at $816E.
Operand of the LDX # at $816D: poll_menu's polls left, stored at $8164; the DEX/BNE after it polls again, and the RTS returns.

27 bytes no code reads: glyph codes $8B-$9C two to a row, nine rows separated by $0D and ended by $00, the layout print_string_direct_at takes for logo_glyph_block. No instruction of the program loads $8173 (searched for the word $8173 and for $73 loaded as an immediate), and with the resident font codes $8B-$9C would draw $C958-$C9E7, the keyboard table and the sound code. Purpose unknown; a leftover by its look.

Sets up the title's menu bar, the only menu this program has: $3E/$3F = $8368 (title_menu_texts), $40/$41 = $836A (title_menu_handlers), menu $3B = 0, bar row $3D = 23, last visible item $3A = 1 (Start and Utils; the credit after them is text), then JMP draw_menu_bar ($02E7). Called once, from startup_main.

Menu 0's bar text, ASCII: 'Start Utils      Written by Alan Pavlish', ended by $00 ($81D5). The items are its words; with $3A = 1 only Start (S) and Utils (U) can be chosen, the rest is Alan Pavlish's credit drawn on the bar.
The hot keys of menu 0's hidden items: none, the list holds only its ending $00 (menu_key reads on from the bar text's $00 at $1BFD).
Menu 0's handler table, a word per item: Start $81FA (menu_start), Utils $81DB (menu_utils). menu_key's run_menu_item ($1C55) calls the chosen one through the JSR it writes at $1C71.

Utils (U): voices 1 and 2 silenced, prepare_for_disk, then $ED = $D7, the masters' identity byte, around check_side_1 ($02D5), so only the original side 1 passes (a play disk holds 0 there and is asked for again); $ED = 0 again; then load_program ($03AD) loads and starts the utilities program, T8/L20. Never returns.

Start (S): voices 1 and 2 silenced; the animation flag $AC kept in the operand at $8280 and the animation turned off; 'Use last saved game (Y/N)?' printed at column 0, row 23 (the bar's row, direct output); then keys until one counts: RETURN or Y use the save on side 1 ($8284), N searches all four sides for the latest save ($8228), the left-arrow key goes back to the title ($827F); other keys are ignored.

N: asks for side 1 (ask_insert_side_1; the left-arrow key cancels), clears the best time so far (the operands at $8246, $824A, $824E, $8253), then for sides 1 to 4 (the operand at $826C) reads that side's saved game (load_save_from_side, which waits until the side is in) and compares its 32-bit game-time count, $04, $05, $06 and $F4FD low byte first (the game adds to it at game $AF61-$AF72, beside its clock update), with the best: when it is not smaller it becomes the best and its side is kept (the operand at $827B). Then the best side's save is loaded again with the game ($828B). Equal counts favour the later side; on fresh disks every count is 0 and side 4 is chosen. Run offline: on the Copy utility's four sides (side 1 saved at count 64, the others 0) it loads side 1; on four sides all at 64, side 4.
Operand of the CMP # at $8245: the low byte ($04) of the latest elapsed time found so far; the LDA $05 after it starts the next byte of the 32-bit comparison.
Operand of the SBC # at $8249: byte 1 ($05) of the latest elapsed time so far; the LDA $06 after it loads byte 2.
Operand of the SBC # at $824D: byte 2 ($06) of the latest elapsed time so far; the LDA $F4FD after it loads the top byte.

Operand of the SBC # at $8252: the top byte ($F4FD) of the latest elapsed time so far. From $8254: a borrow (this side's time is smaller) skips to the next side; otherwise $04, $05, $06 and $F4FD are stored into the four operands as the new best, and the side follows.
Operand of the LDA # at $826B: the side being read, 1 to 4, stored at $823D. From $826D: it becomes the best side (into the operand at $827B); then $8270-$8278 count the side up and loop until 5.
Operand of the LDA # at $827A: the side holding the latest save so far (stored at $826D), passed in A to load_save_and_game by the JMP after it.
Back to the title from Start: $AC = the animation flag menu_start kept in this LDA's operand ($8280), RTS to menu_key, which redraws the bar.
Operand of the LDA # at $827F: the animation flag $AC as it was when Start was chosen (stored at $8202); the STA $AC and RTS after it put it back.
Y or RETURN: asks for side 1 (ask_insert_side_1; the left-arrow key cancels to start_cancel), then A = 1 and on into load_save_and_game.

Loads the saved game of side A (load_save_from_side), makes the item table load (DEC $76, so that $76 differs from $75, then load_item_table $03BC, which loads file $75: 0, from the start-up's clear of zero page), waits for side 1 (check_side_1 $02D5) and loads and starts the game at T31/L9 (load_program $03AD). Never returns.

Prints 'Insert side 1. (RETURN)' at column 0, row 23 (direct output) and JMP wait_return ($03EF): carry clear for RETURN or space, set for the left-arrow key. It checks nothing itself; the side check comes after (check_disk_side).
ASCII 'Insert side 1. (RETURN)', then $03 (clear to the end of the line) and $00; printed by ask_insert_side_1.

Reads the saved game of disk side A: redraws the bar over the prompt (draw_menu_bar $02E7), prepare_for_disk, waits for side A (check_disk_side $02DB, which asks 'INSERT SIDE n. (RETURN)' until that side is in, with no way out), then JMP read_saved_game.
ASCII 'Use last saved game (', $01 (inverse on), 'Y', $02 (inverse off), '/N)?', $03 (clear to the end of the line), $00: the prompt menu_start prints, with Y the inverse default.

Readies the engine for leaving the title: animation off, message area cleared (clear_text_area), $92 = 1 (the game's entry code tests it at game $7E5C and then calls the game's $AE21, after entering the first map), anim_channel_enables[0] ($5BFB) = 1 (picture animation channel 0 enabled), and the picture flags $B8, $AC and $C5 = 0. Called by menu_utils and load_save_from_side.

Reads the saved game from the disk in the drive: pages 0-7 from track 35, logical sectors 7 down to 0, to $F400-$FBFF (read_save_page $02CF, the page in the operand at $8319; its BCS at $8316 would return early, but read_save_page goes through disk_io, which retries until the read works). Then unscrambles and checks it ($8321), and puts the saved zero page back ($834E). Returns carry clear.

Operand of the LDA # at $8318: the page being read, 0-7, stored at $8310; the ADC/CMP/BCC after it reads the next page until all eight are in. saved_game_bad_checksum keeps its page, 0-7, in the same byte (stored at $8331, read at $8344).

Unscrambles the eight pages with the key in $F4FF (scramble_save $04E7: each byte 0-$FE EORed with twice its offset and the key) and compares their checksum (save_checksum $04EA) with $F4FF: a match goes on to $834E.

A checksum that does not match is accepted anyway: each byte 0-$FE of the eight pages is EORed again with twice its offset (page in the operand at $8319, selected with select_character $0338), which leaves the bytes as stored EORed with $F4FF alone. A save written in the clear with $F4FF = 0 comes out unchanged; what this was meant for is not known. Run offline with one byte of a save flipped: every byte of $F400-$FBFF then held the stored byte EOR $F4FF (offsets $FF as stored), except the line buffer $F49C-$F4C4, which restore_saved_zero_page clears, and the start-up went on towards the game (to load_program) with no message.

Copies the saved zero page $F478-$F485 back to $02-$0F (among them the view's top-left square $02/$03 and the map $09, which the game sets before enter_map at game $8A1E-$8A28; the game-time count $04-$06, whose top byte is $F4FD; the clock's minutes $0D and hours $0E, game $AF3D-$AF56; and the text speed $0F), empties the line buffer (clear_line_buffer $04ED, which zeroes $F49C-$F4C4 inside the save's first page) and returns carry clear.
Picture animation off: $AC = 0, so animate_picture_tick does nothing. The BIT $01A9 at $8362 hides animation_on's LDA #$01.
Picture animation on: $AC = 1; entered inside the BIT at $8362.
The bar text table that $3E/$3F point at (setup_title_menu): one word, menu 0's text, $81AD (title_bar_text).
The handler-table table that $40/$41 point at: one word, menu 0's handlers, $81D7 (title_handlers).

Colours the picture area: screen matrix rows 1-16, columns 1-36 (screen_row_address $0502 for each row) = $86, so in multicolour bitmap mode its pixel pairs %01 show colour 8 and %10 colour 6 (the matrix byte's high and low nibbles). Called by startup_main ($7F78) before the frame, the logo and the picture are drawn, and after each redraw of the picture by attract_loop ($8033, $806A).

Exchanges the font's glyphs $20-$5F ($C600-$C7FF) with the logo glyphs at $CA00-$CBFF, byte for byte. startup_main calls it before and after printing the logo ($7FB1, $7FD7), so the resident font ends as it began and $CA00-$CBFF keeps the logo.

The logo's layout for print_string_direct_at: glyph codes $20-$5F four to a row, 16 rows each ended by $0D except the last, ended by $00. Printed at column 33, row 1 while the logo font is swapped in, it draws the letters of WASTELAND one under another, upright, down columns 33-36, with a small white mark beside the D (logo_font, $CA00).

Types message A of the start-up's text at column X, row Y, a character at a time: direct output; finds the engine's print_char JMP ($1DF8, through the jump table's $0323 entry, print_vector_ptr), copies its target (the direct printer $1F03) into the JSR at $8424 and points the JMP at type_char_hook; then print_message ($0311) with $43/$44 = $8478. The hook stays until output is selected again (show_title_message's output_wrapped, or the engine's output_direct).
Each character of a typed message: printed through the routine type_message_at saved in this JSR's operand ($8425/$8426); then the pause and the poll ($8427).
Low byte of the JSR operand at $8424, written by type_message_at ($840C): the print routine that was in print_char ($03 of $1F03 in this snapshot).
High byte of the JSR operand at $8424, written at $8416 ($1F in this snapshot).

After each typed character: the engine's click (play_sound_16 via $04D2), delay_a($A0), one keyboard poll (poll_menu, X = 1) with $31/$32 and the text cursor and window kept around it (push_zp23 $0247, pull_zp23 $024C), then print_char pointed at type_char_hook again, since a menu handler run from the poll may have selected other output.

$12/$13 = the operand of the jump table's print_char entry (the JMP at $0323, so $0324/$0325 = $1DF8): the engine's own print_char JMP, whose operand is the current output routine. Used by type_message_at and type_char_pause.
records.s: $0324/$0325: the operand of the engine's jump-table JMP at $0323, print_char $1DF8 (not the KERNAL's input vector here)

records.c: Unused entry: $23 = X, $24 = Y, then on into show_title_message. No instruction calls $8460 (searched the program for the word $8460), and show_message keeps its own cursor in any case.

Shows message A of the start-up's text in the message area: word-wrapped output (output_wrapped $0302), $43/$44 = $8478 (select_title_text), JMP show_message ($0326). The credits and messages 8-12 of attract_loop.

records.s: engine entry $0326 = show_message (not the KERNAL's output vector here)

records.c: Points $43/$44 at the start-up's packed text block, $8478 (title_text). A kept.

The start-up's packed text block, base $8478 (select_title_text): its 60-byte alphabet, code n reading the byte at $8478+n: ' teanoisrd' (0-9), $00 (10, the end code), 'cpl' $0D 'umhwyf:8.91vg!b' (11-29); codes $1E and $1F capitalise and escape, and the escape reaches '6' '-' ''' (30-32) and $7F filler (33-59). Messages 1-17 are used; the group comments below give their text. Run offline through every title path, the program reads $8478-$8498 and $84B4-$860A of the block and nothing after $860A.

The block's group table at base+$3C: five words, offsets from $84B4 to each group of four messages: $000A ($84BE), $0051 ($8505), $0093 ($8547), $00FB ($85AF), $0132 ($85E6). find_message ($1E0E) reads it.

'; 3 '               WASTELAND!
' (the credits).
Messages 4-7, to $8546: 4 'Copyright 1986-88 Interplay Productions.\n'; 5 'Place : EARTH'; 6 'Year  : 1998'; 7 'Status: DEFCON 1' (5-7 typed over the picture).

Messages 8-11, to $85AE: 8 '
 Computer defense initiative activated.
'; 9 '
  Diplomatic solutions to the world's

'.
Messages 12-15, to $85E5: 12 '  dreams.\n'; 13 'Current condition:'; 14 'High concentrations of'; 15 'radiation produce random storms'.

Messages 16 and 17, to $860A: 16 'and mutations. Somehow life'; 17 'continues in the Wasteland!'. The group's last two slots, 18 and 19, would decode from the stale bytes after it; nothing asks for them.
